screens.heading: You are safe here
screens.reassurance: This module will not request any rides or share your location. You are just reading.
screens.goal: By the end of this module, you will know how to request an Uber safely, verify your driver before getting in, and feel confident using ride-sharing for appointments, errands, or travel.

screens.heading: Robert's story
body: Robert, 76, had always driven himself everywhere. When his car went in for a week-long repair, he needed to get to a doctor's appointment across town. His daughter suggested Uber.

'I do not want a stranger driving me around,' Robert said. His daughter showed him how it worked — you see the driver's name, photo, car model, and licence plate before they arrive. This driver had 4.9 stars over 2,000 trips.

The driver arrived on time. Robert checked the licence plate against the app — a match. He made his appointment with ten minutes to spare. 'It is actually more comfortable than a taxi,' he says. 'And I feel safer because I can see everything before I get in.'
screens.tellMeMore: Ride-sharing is not hailing a random taxi. Uber and Lyft drivers are screened, rated, and tracked by GPS throughout your ride. Every trip is recorded — the route, the driver, the time. Your family can share your live location. If anything goes wrong, there is a full digital trail and in-app emergency support.

screens.heading: Requesting an Uber — step by step
body: Open the Uber app. Your current location appears automatically on the map. Tap 'Where to?' and type your destination.

The app shows you available cars nearby, the estimated arrival time (usually 2–8 minutes), and the price upfront. Tap 'Request.' A driver accepts and their details appear: name, photo, car model, colour, and licence plate.

Wait outside when the car is 1–2 minutes away. Before getting in: check the licence plate matches the app. The driver will confirm your name. If either does not match — do not get in. Cancel and request another.
screens.tellMeMore: You can also share your trip with a family member from within the app. Tap 'Share status' and send them a link — they can watch your trip live on their phone. This is a reassuring feature for both you and your family. Payment is automatic — your card is charged at the end of the trip. You never need cash.

screens.heading: Staying safe every ride
body: The three checks before getting in: (1) licence plate matches the app, (2) car make and colour matches, (3) driver says your name without being asked. All three should match.
Sit in the back seat. This gives you more personal space and an easier exit.
If you ever feel unsafe during a ride: the app has a safety button (a shield icon). Tap it to share your location with emergency services or call 911 directly.
screens.tellMeMore: After every ride, you rate the driver (1–5 stars) and they rate you. High-rated drivers are the most reliable. If a ride is exceptional, add a cash tip or tip through the app. If a driver is unprofessional — even slightly — give them fewer stars and leave a note. This keeps the service quality high for everyone.

screens.heading: Getting the Uber app set up
body: Download Uber from the App Store (iPhone/iPad) or Google Play (Android). Create a free account with your email address. Add a credit or debit card — your card number is encrypted and never shown again.
Lyft is the main alternative to Uber in Canada. It works identically. Some cities have more Uber drivers; others have more Lyft. Having both apps installed gives you options.
You can set up Uber on your behalf for an elderly parent: Uber for Family lets you add family members, pay for their rides, and see their trip status from your own phone.
screens.tellMeMore: If you are not comfortable with apps, Uber has a phone option in some cities — you call a number and a dispatcher books the ride for you. Ask a family member or library staff to help you find this option in your area. Some municipalities also have senior-specific ride programmes that partner with Uber — your local library or senior centre can help you find these.

screens.heading: You now have a driver on demand
takeaways: Before getting in: check licence plate, car details, and that the driver says your first name. All three must match.
Sit in the back seat. The app's safety button connects you to emergency services instantly.
Payment is automatic — no cash needed. The price is shown before you confirm.
Share your trip with a family member so they can watch you travel in real time.
Uber for Family lets a family member pay for and monitor your rides.
screens.confidence: You can now request, verify, and complete a safe Uber ride — to any appointment, errand, or destination.
